propositions: Long-running gate operations emit no progress signal to stdout/stderr between start and final verdict, causing supervisor watchdogs with standard 600s budgets to kill healthy runs mid-close.

Gate operations routinely exceed 600s duration (measured 27–146s per call) with substantial silent periods during local compute phases (prologue, overlap retrieval), not explained by model latency alone.
An autonomous agent orchestrating an epic close was killed mid-verification when no output arrived for 600s, leaving the epic and stories stranded in-progress despite all code changes landing.
ADR 0089 and test suite encode that gate operations intentionally tolerate silence and have no total-runtime timer, making progress output a feature-request rather than a bug fix.

Remedy options include periodic stderr heartbeat emission (compatible with blocking sync code via threading, per _heartbeat.py pattern), streaming/chunked model interaction, or documentation warning operators to raise supervisor budgets deliberately.
